newsitem.title: USA: Kodak tumbles after Q2 earnings disappoint.
newsitem.headline: Kodak tumbles after Q2 earnings disappoint.

text.p: Shares in Eastman Kodak Co tumbled on Wednesday after the imaging giant posted second quarter earnings well below Wall Street expectations.
The stock, one of the 30 Dow Jones Industrial Average components, opened on New York Stock Exchange at 67-1/2 down 9-3/8. It later recovered some ground and was off 8-15/16 at 67-15/16.
Before the stock market opening, Kodak posted second quarter earnings of $1.12 a share, below First Call's consensus expectation of $1.39.

"The story is that the company booted the earnings badly, and that earnings are going to be flat for the full year and probably not rebound that much in 1998," said Prudential Securities analyst Alex Henderson.
Henderson attributed Kodak's woes to a market share loss stemming from a price war with film rival Fuji Photo Film Co .
"The market share loss that Kodak is experiencing is definitely cutting into their results," he said.
He downgraded his rating on Kodak to hold from buy and cut his 1997 earnings per share estimate $4.40 from $4.85 and his 1998 forecast to $4.75 from $5.65.
Kodak said its second quarter results were hurt by the strong U.S. dollar, growing losses for digital products, higher marketing expenses and price competition.

Kodak chief executive George Fisher said in a statement that it will be "very difficult" for Kodak to grow its 1997 operating earnings per share beyond 1996 levels. The company earned $4.50 a share from continuing operations in 1996.
